The integrity of restored assets is verified, systems and services are restored, and normal operating status is confirmed.
End of incident recovery is declared and documentation completed
The end of incident recovery is declared based on criteria, and incident-related documentation is completed.
Recovery progress is communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders
Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to designated internal and external stakeholders.
Public updates on incident recovery use approved methods and messaging
Public updates on incident recovery are shared using approved methods and messaging.

g: Chapter IV - Cybersecurity risk-management measures and reporting obligations
r: Submit entity information for the national list of entities
Give the competent authority name, address, contacts, IP ranges, sector and Member States served; notify changes within two weeks.
Management body approves, oversees and is liable for risk-management measures
Have the management body approve the Article 21 measures, oversee their implementation and accept accountability for infringements.
Cybersecurity training for management body members and staff
Management body members must follow training; offer similar training to employees regularly.
Appropriate and proportionate cybersecurity risk-management measures
Take technical, operational and organisational measures proportionate to risk exposure, size, likelihood and severity of incidents.
Policies on risk analysis and information system security
Adopt policies for risk analysis and the security of information systems.
Establish incident handling capabilities and procedures.
Business continuity, backup management, disaster recovery and crisis management
Maintain business continuity and DR arrangements, backups and crisis management.
Address security in relationships with direct suppliers and service providers.
Secure acquisition, development and maintenance; vulnerability handling and disclosure
Build security into system acquisition, development and maintenance and handle and disclose vulnerabilities.
Policies and procedures to assess effectiveness of risk-management measures
Measure and assess whether cybersecurity risk-management measures are effective.
Basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training
Apply basic cyber hygiene and provide cybersecurity training.
Policies and procedures on cryptography and encryption
Define rules for cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption.
Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
Apply HR security, access control policies and asset management.
MFA or continuous authentication, secured communications and emergency communications
Use MFA or continuous authentication and secured voice, video, text and emergency communication where appropriate.
Consider supplier-specific vulnerabilities and coordinated supply chain risk assessments
Assess each direct supplier's vulnerabilities, product quality and secure development, and EU coordinated supply chain assessments.
Take corrective measures for non-compliance with Article 21(2)
Where measures are found non-compliant, take corrective action without undue delay.
Notify significant incidents to the CSIRT or authority and inform affected recipients
Notify significant incidents without undue delay, include cross-border impact information, and inform affected service recipients.
Communicate measures to recipients potentially affected by a significant cyber threat
Tell potentially affected recipients what measures or remedies they can take and, where appropriate, about the threat.
Determine whether an incident is significant
Classify incidents as significant where they cause severe disruption or loss, or considerable damage to others.
Within 24 hours of awareness, send an early warning stating suspected malicious cause and possible cross-border impact.
Within 72 hours, update the early warning with an initial assessment, severity, impact and IoCs (trust service providers: 24 hours).
Provide an intermediate status report when the CSIRT or competent authority requests it.
Within one month of the notification, report description, severity, root cause, mitigation and cross-border impact.
If the incident is ongoing at the final report date, give a progress report and a final report within one month of handling it.
Inform the public about a significant incident when required
Inform the public where the CSIRT or competent authority requires it after consulting the entity.
Use certified ICT products, services and processes where required
Use ICT products, services and processes certified under EU schemes where the Member State requires it; use qualified trust services.
Use European and international standards and technical specifications
Align security measures with relevant European and international standards as encouraged by the Member State.
Submit registration information to the competent authority
Digital infrastructure and digital provider entities submit name, sector, establishments, contacts, Member States served and IP ranges.
Notify changes to registration information within three months
Notify the competent authority of any change to submitted information without delay and within three months.
Collect and maintain accurate domain name registration data
TLD registries and registrars keep accurate, complete registration data in a dedicated database, respecting data protection law.
Verification policies and procedures for registration data
Have published policies and verification procedures ensuring registration data is accurate and complete.
Publish non-personal domain name registration data
Make non-personal registration data public without undue delay after registration.
Answer lawful access requests for registration data within 72 hours
Give legitimate access seekers specific data on lawful, substantiated requests within 72 hours; publish disclosure policies.
Cooperate to avoid duplicate collection of registration data
TLD registries and registrars cooperate so registration data is not collected twice.
Notify participation in cybersecurity information-sharing arrangements
Tell the competent authority when joining or withdrawing from information-sharing arrangements.
Voluntary notification of incidents, cyber threats and near misses
Optionally notify the CSIRT or authority of incidents, cyber threats and near misses beyond Article 23 duties.
Essential entities: submit to on-site inspections and off-site supervision
Support on-site inspections, off-site supervision and random checks by the competent authority.
Essential entities: regular and targeted security audits
Undergo regular and targeted independent security audits, pay their cost and share results with the authority.
Undergo ad hoc audits, e.g. after a significant incident or infringement.
Cooperate with risk-based security scans by the authority.
Essential entities: information requests on risk-management measures
Provide information on risk-management measures, documented policies and Article 27 registration compliance on request.
Essential entities: access to data, documents and information
Give the authority access to data, documents and information needed for supervision.
Essential entities: evidence of implementation of cybersecurity policies
Provide evidence such as qualified auditor results and underlying evidence on request.
Essential entities: comply with enforcement measures
Act on warnings, binding instructions, orders, audit recommendations and any monitoring officer within set deadlines.
Legal representatives able to ensure compliance and liable for breaches
Persons representing or controlling the entity must have power to ensure compliance and can be held liable.
Important entities: on-site inspections and off-site ex post supervision
Support on-site inspections and ex post off-site supervision.
Undergo targeted independent security audits, pay their cost and share results with the authority.
Cooperate with risk-based security scans by the authority.
Important entities: information requests on risk-management measures
Provide information to assess, ex post, risk-management measures, documented policies and registration compliance.
Important entities: access to data, documents and information
Give the authority access to data, documents and information needed for supervision.
Important entities: evidence of implementation of cybersecurity policies
Provide evidence such as qualified auditor results and underlying evidence on request.
Important entities: comply with enforcement measures
Act on warnings, binding instructions, orders and audit recommendations within set deadlines.

r: Take size, risk profile and complexity into account
Scale ICT security policies and the simplified framework to size, overall risk profile and complexity of services.
ICT security policies embedded in the ICT risk management framework
Set ICT security policies, procedures, protocols and tools covering network security, intrusion safeguards, data CIA and reliable transmission.
Required content of ICT security policies
Align with strategy, record management approval date, set indicators, staff duties, segregation of duties, documentation and review.
Record approval of the ICT risk tolerance level set under DORA Art. 6(8)(b).
ICT risk assessment procedure and methodology
Define how threats and vulnerabilities are identified and how impact and likelihood are measured.
Identify, implement and document treatment measures to bring ICT risk within tolerance and monitor their effectiveness.
Residual ICT risk acceptance, inventory and annual review
Assign acceptance roles, keep an inventory of accepted residual risks with justification and review it at least yearly.
Monitoring of ICT risk and the threat landscape
Monitor changes in ICT risk, threats and internal and external vulnerabilities to detect risk-profile changes promptly.
Reflect changes in business and resilience strategy
Have a process to take changes to business and digital operational resilience strategy into account.
Develop, document and implement a policy for managing the lifecycle of classified ICT assets.
Records kept for each ICT asset
Record identifier, location, classification, owner, supported functions, RTO/RPO, external exposure, dependencies and support end dates.
Records for legacy ICT system risk assessment
Entities other than microenterprises keep records needed to risk-assess legacy ICT systems.
ICT asset management procedure and criticality assessment
Define criteria for assessing criticality of information and ICT assets based on business-function dependencies and CIA impact.
Policy on encryption and cryptographic controls
Develop, document and implement an encryption and cryptographic controls policy.
Encryption rules for data at rest, in transit, in use and network traffic
Base rules on data classification and risk assessment; protect data in use in a separated environment where encryption is not possible.
Select techniques using leading practices and standards; apply mitigation and monitoring where they cannot be followed.
Update cryptographic technology based on cryptanalysis
Provide for changing cryptographic technology as cryptanalysis develops, or adopt mitigating measures.
Record and justify cryptographic mitigation measures
Record any mitigation and monitoring measures adopted under 6(3)-(4) with a reasoned explanation.
Manage keys through generation, renewal, storage, backup, archiving, retrieval, transmission, retirement, revocation and destruction.
Protect cryptographic keys against loss and unauthorised access
Implement controls protecting keys throughout their lifecycle, designed on classification and risk assessment.
Replace lost, compromised or damaged keys
Develop methods to replace keys that are lost, compromised or damaged.
Register of certificates and certificate-storing devices
Keep an up-to-date register of certificates and devices, at least for assets supporting critical or important functions.
Prompt renewal of certificates before expiry
Renew certificates in advance of their expiration.
Policies and procedures for ICT operations
Document how ICT assets are operated, monitored, controlled and restored.
Secure installation, configuration and legacy system control
Set requirements for installing, configuring and decommissioning systems, handling information assets and controlling legacy systems.
Controls and monitoring of ICT systems
Cover backup and restore, scheduling, audit trails and logs, and separation of production from development and test, with approved production testing.
Error handling, escalation and restart procedures
Define error handling, support and escalation contacts, and restart, rollback and recovery procedures.
Identify capacity needs, optimise resources and monitor availability, efficiency and capacity shortages.
Develop, document and implement vulnerability management procedures, recording and tracking all detected vulnerabilities.
Automated vulnerability scanning, weekly for critical assets
Scan ICT assets with frequency based on classification; at least weekly for assets supporting critical or important functions.
Check providers handle and report critical vulnerabilities and require root-cause investigation and mitigation.
Track usage and versions of third-party and open-source libraries in services supporting critical or important functions.
Establish procedures to disclose vulnerabilities responsibly to clients, counterparties and the public.
Develop, document and implement patch management procedures.
Patch identification, emergency patching, testing and deadlines
Use automated tools to find patches, set emergency procedures, test before deployment and set deadlines with escalation.
Develop, document and implement a data and system security procedure aligned to classification.
Apply Article 21 access restrictions supporting protection for each classification level.
Define secure baselines for ICT assets using leading practices and verify regularly that they are deployed.
Ensure only authorised software is installed on systems and endpoints.
Identify and implement security measures against malicious code.
Only authorised storage media, systems and endpoints
Allow only authorised media, systems and endpoint devices to transfer and store entity data.
Secure portable and private endpoint devices
Use remote management and wipe, tamper-proof security mechanisms and restrict removable media to tolerated risk.
Secure deletion of data no longer needed
Securely delete data held on premises or externally that is no longer needed.
Securely dispose of or decommission storage devices containing confidential information.
Implement measures preventing data loss and leakage on systems and endpoints.
Ensure teleworking and private endpoints do not weaken ICT security.
Resilience requirements for third-party operated ICT assets
Apply vendor settings, allocate security responsibilities, keep in-house competence and reduce provider infrastructure risk.
Develop, document and implement logging as a safeguard against intrusion and misuse.
Define events to log and log retention
Identify events to log, set retention based on objectives and risk assessment, and secure log handling.
Log access, capacity, change, operations and network events
Log events for access control and identity, capacity, change, ICT operations and network traffic.
Protect logs against tampering and unauthorised access
Protect logging systems and log data at rest, in transit and in use.
Implement measures to detect failure of logging systems.
Clock synchronisation to a reliable time source
Synchronise clocks of all ICT systems to a documented reliable reference time source.
Segregation and segmentation of systems and networks
Segment networks based on function criticality, classification and asset risk profile.
Document network connections and data flows
Document all network connections and data flows.
Use a separate dedicated network for administering ICT assets.
Network access control against unauthorised devices
Prevent and detect connections by unauthorised or non-compliant devices and endpoints.
Encrypt connections over corporate, public, domestic, third-party and wireless networks based on classification and risk.
Design networks to meet ICT security requirements and leading practices for CIA.
Secure traffic between internal networks and the internet
Secure traffic between internal networks, the internet and other external connections.
Firewall rule management and review (6-monthly for critical systems)
Define roles for firewall rules and filters and review them regularly; at least every 6 months for critical systems.
Annual review of network architecture and security design
Review network architecture and security design yearly (periodically for microenterprises).
Temporary isolation of subnetworks and devices
Be able to isolate subnetworks, components and devices where necessary.
Secure baseline and hardening of network components
Harden network devices in line with vendor instructions, standards and leading practices.
Session timeout for system and remote sessions
Limit, lock and terminate inactive system and remote sessions.
Security requirements in network services agreements
Specify security measures, service levels and management requirements for all network services.
Protect information in transit and prevent leakage
Ensure CIA of data in transmission, detect and prevent leaks and transfer data securely to external parties.
Implement, document and regularly review confidentiality agreements for staff and third parties.
Set a policy covering objectives, governance, planning, risk assessment, milestones, change and security testing of ICT projects.
Report critical ICT projects to the management body
Report progress and risks of projects affecting critical or important functions periodically and when needed.
Policy on ICT systems acquisition, development and maintenance
Define security practices, approved security requirements and anti-tampering measures for ICT systems.
Test and approve ICT systems before use and after maintenance
Test and approve systems commensurate to criticality; CCPs and CSDs involve relevant participants.
Source code reviews with static and dynamic testing
Analyse source code vulnerabilities, adopt an action plan and monitor it; security-test internet-exposed systems.
Security testing of software packages at integration
Security-test software packages no later than the integration phase.
Only anonymised or pseudonymised data in non-production
Store only anonymised, pseudonymised or randomised production data outside production and protect it.
Approved, time-limited use of production data for testing
Allow production data in testing only for specific, approved, time-limited occasions reported to ICT risk management.
Implement controls protecting source code integrity, including code delivered by providers.
Analyse third-party and open-source code before deployment
Test proprietary software and provider or open-source code before production deployment.
Apply development controls to end-user developed systems
Apply Article 16 controls risk-based to ICT systems built or managed outside the ICT function.
Verify security requirements, define roles, document and communicate changes, set fall-back and assess security impact.
Independence of change approval from request and implementation
Separate the functions approving changes from those requesting and implementing them.
Manage emergency changes with adequate safeguards.
Document, re-evaluate, assess and approve emergency changes, workarounds and patches after implementation.
CCPs and CSDs stress-test systems after significant changes
Submit ICT systems to stringent testing simulating stressed conditions after significant changes.
Specify, document and implement a policy based on threat landscape, classification and asset risk profile.
Protect premises and data centres from attacks and hazards
Protect premises, data centres and sensitive areas commensurate with their importance.
Secure ICT assets inside and outside premises
Secure ICT assets on and off premises, including unattended assets; maintain physical security devices.
Apply a clear desk policy for papers and a clear screen policy.
Assign ICT security responsibilities in HR policy
Identify and assign specific ICT security responsibilities.
Staff and providers informed of and adhere to ICT security policies
Require staff and provider personnel accessing ICT assets to know and follow ICT security policies.
Awareness of reporting channels for anomalous behaviour
Make staff aware of channels to report anomalous behaviour, including whistleblowing channels.
Require staff to return all ICT and tangible information assets on leaving.
Uniquely identify and authenticate persons and systems accessing information.
Unique identity per user and records of assignments
Assign a unique account to each staff member and provider user; keep identity assignment records.
Manage creation, change, review, deactivation and termination of all accounts, automated where feasible.
Assign access rights on least privilege, including for remote and emergency access.
Segregation of duties in access rights
Prevent toxic combinations of access rights and unjustified access to critical data.
User accountability and limits on generic accounts
Limit generic and shared accounts so users are always identifiable.
Controls and tools preventing unauthorised access
Restrict access to ICT assets with controls and tools against unauthorised access.
Privileged, emergency and admin access on need-to-use basis
Grant privileged access ad hoc, use dedicated admin accounts and automate privileged access management where feasible.
Withdraw access without undue delay on termination or when no longer needed.
Access rights review yearly, 6-monthly for critical systems
Update access rights at least yearly, and every 6 months for systems supporting critical functions.
Use authentication matched to classification; strong authentication for remote, privileged, critical and public-facing access.
Identify, log, grant on least privilege, monitor and review physical access to premises and data centres.
Document the ICT-related incident management process
Document the incident management process required by DORA Art. 17.
Contacts list for ICT operations security
Keep internal and external contacts for threat monitoring, anomaly detection and vulnerability management.
Operate technical, organisational and operational mechanisms for prompt detection of anomalies.
Retain incident evidence securely and no longer than necessary.
Analyse significant or recurring incidents and patterns in incident occurrence.
Roles for detecting and responding to incidents
Set clear roles and responsibilities for detection and response.
Collect and analyse logs, threats and provider notifications, alert on anomalies and prioritise alerts in and out of hours.
Protect anomaly records against tampering and unauthorised access.
Log occurrence, detection time and type of anomalies
Log date and time of occurrence and detection and the type of each anomalous activity.
Criteria to trigger incident detection and response
Consider malicious activity, data losses, transaction impact, unavailability and service criticality as triggers.
Components of the ICT business continuity policy
Define objectives, scope, activation criteria, governance, recovery objectives, plan testing and alignment with communication policy.
CCP business continuity requirements (2-hour recovery, secondary site)
CCPs set a maximum 2-hour recovery for critical functions and keep a distinct secondary processing site.
CSDs consider interdependencies and ensure RTO for critical functions is at most 2 hours.
Trading venues resume trading within about 2 hours with near-zero data loss.
Base BCP testing on BIA and ICT risk assessment
Take the business impact analysis and ICT risk assessment into account when testing.
BCP test scenarios incl. providers and switchover
Test severe but plausible scenarios, provider services and failure, switchover to redundant capacity, and staff response.
CCPs involve clearing members and providers in BCP tests
CCPs involve clearing members, external providers and interdependent institutions in testing.
CSDs involve users and infrastructures in BCP tests
CSDs involve users, critical utilities, other CSDs and market infrastructures as appropriate.
Document BCP test results and report deficiencies
Document results; analyse, fix and report deficiencies to the management body.
ICT response and recovery plan content
Define activation conditions, recovery actions and objectives, accessible documentation, roles and short and long-term options.
Cover cyber-attacks, provider failure, premises and asset failure, staff loss, climate, insider, political and power outage scenarios.
Consider alternatives where primary recovery is not feasible in the short term.
Continuity measures for failure of critical ICT providers
Implement continuity measures mitigating failure of providers supporting critical or important functions.
Submit ICT risk management framework review report electronically
Submit the review report under DORA Art. 6(5) in a searchable electronic format.
Content of the framework review report
Include context, approval date, review reason and period, findings, remediation measures, past reviews and sources.
Internal governance and control framework for ICT risk
Have an internal governance and control framework ensuring prudent ICT risk management.
Management body responsibilities under the simplified framework
Management body sets roles and objectives, approves classifications and BCPs, allocates budget yearly and sets reporting.
Remain responsible when outsourcing compliance verification
Stay fully responsible for verifying ICT risk compliance even where verification is outsourced.
Segregation and independence of control and audit functions
Ensure control functions and internal audit are segregated and independent.
Internal audit of the simplified framework
Audit the framework by competent, independent auditors at a risk-based frequency.
Timely remediation of critical ICT audit findings
Verify and remediate critical ICT audit findings in a timely manner.
Document high-level principles protecting data and service CIA and authenticity.
ICT security measures based on the policy
Implement Articles 30-38 measures, including those implemented by ICT providers.
Identify and classify critical functions and supporting assets
Identify, classify and document critical or important functions, supporting assets and interdependencies.
Identify critical functions supported by ICT providers
Identify all critical or important functions supported by ICT third-party providers.
Set tolerance, assess risks, define and monitor mitigation, and assess risk after major change, tests or incidents.
Carry out and document risk assessments periodically per the ICT risk profile.
Monitor threats and vulnerabilities to critical functions and assets; review risk scenarios regularly.
Alert thresholds to trigger incident response
Set alert thresholds and criteria that trigger incident response.
Protect premises and data centres from unauthorised access, attacks, accidents and environmental hazards.
Logical and physical access control procedures
Apply least privilege, accountability, account management, strong authentication and periodic access review.
Monitor and manage ICT asset lifecycle
Monitor and manage the lifecycle of all ICT assets.
Monitor provider support of ICT assets
Monitor whether ICT assets remain supported by ICT providers.
Identify capacity needs and prevent ICT capacity shortages.
Scan assets according to classification and deploy patches for identified vulnerabilities.
Manage outdated, unsupported or legacy ICT assets
Manage risks from outdated, unsupported or legacy ICT assets.
Log access, operations, network and change events
Log access control, ICT operations, traffic and change management events.
Monitor anomalous activities for critical operations
Monitor and analyse anomalous activity for critical or important ICT operations.
Monitor relevant, up-to-date cyber threat information.
Detect leakage, malicious code and known vulnerabilities
Identify information leakage, malware and publicly known vulnerabilities and check for updates.
Protect data in use, in transit and at rest
Implement measures protecting data in use, in transit and at rest.
Secure software, storage media, systems and endpoints
Secure software, media, systems and endpoints that transfer and store entity data.
Prevent unauthorised network connections and secure external traffic
Prevent and detect unauthorised connections and secure internet and external traffic.
Ensure CIA and authenticity of data in network transmission.
Secure deletion of data no longer needed
Securely delete data on premises or stored externally that is no longer needed.
Securely dispose of or decommission storage devices with confidential information.
Ensure teleworking and private devices do not impair critical activities.
Establish a plan testing the effectiveness of security measures, considering identified threats and vulnerabilities.
Review, assess and test ICT security measures
Test security measures considering the risk profile of ICT assets.
Evaluate results and update measures without undue delay for critical systems.
ICT systems acquisition, development and maintenance procedure
Approve requirements incl. security before acquisition, test before use and changes, and prevent tampering.
Document a project procedure covering initiation to closure with defined roles.
Record, test, assess, approve, implement and verify all ICT changes in a controlled way.
ICT business continuity plans based on severe disruption analysis
Develop BCPs from exposure analysis of severe disruptions, including cyber-attack scenarios.
Content of ICT business continuity plans
Approve plans, allocate resources, set recovery levels, backup scope and frequency, communications and update triggers.
Annual testing of business continuity plans
Test BCPs incl. backup and restore at least yearly and on major change.
Testing must show business viability until critical operations are restored and identify deficiencies.
Document BCP test results and report deficiencies
Document results; analyse, fix and report deficiencies to the management body.
Submit simplified framework review report electronically
Submit the review report in a searchable electronic format.
Content of the simplified framework review report
Include context, approval, review reasons and period, findings, remediation and conclusions.
Internal governance and control framework for ICT risk
Have an internal governance and control framework for effective and prudent ICT risk management.
Management body defines, approves, oversees and is responsible for the ICT risk framework
Management body bears ultimate responsibility for ICT risk and sets policies, roles and governance.
Approve the digital operational resilience strategy and ICT risk tolerance
Set and approve the resilience strategy, including the ICT risk tolerance level.
Approve and review ICT business continuity policy and recovery plans
Approve and periodically review the ICT BC policy and response and recovery plans.
Approve and review ICT internal audit plans
Approve and periodically review ICT internal audit plans, audits and material changes.
Allocate budget for resilience, awareness and ICT skills
Allocate and periodically review budget for resilience needs, training and ICT skills.
Approve the policy on use of ICT third-party services
Approve and periodically review the policy on ICT services from third-party providers.
Reporting channels on third-party arrangements and major incidents
Be informed of third-party arrangements, planned material changes and major ICT incidents.
Role to monitor ICT third-party arrangements
Non-microenterprises set a monitoring role or senior manager accountable for third-party ICT risk.
Management body ICT risk knowledge and training
Management body members keep sufficient ICT risk knowledge through regular training.
Sound, comprehensive and documented ICT risk management framework
Maintain a documented ICT risk framework as part of overall risk management.
Framework protects information and ICT assets and physical components
Include strategies, policies, procedures, protocols and tools protecting all assets incl. premises and data centres.
Minimise ICT risk impact and inform authorities on request
Minimise ICT risk impact and provide complete ICT risk information to authorities on request.
Independent ICT risk control function and three lines of defence
Assign ICT risk to an independent control function; segregate management, control and audit.
Annual review of the ICT risk framework and review report
Review at least yearly and after major incidents, instructions or findings; give the report on request.
Regular internal audit of the ICT risk framework
Non-microenterprises have the framework audited regularly by competent, independent auditors.
Follow-up of critical ICT audit findings
Have a formal follow-up process for timely remediation of critical audit findings.
Define a strategy covering risk tolerance, security objectives and KPIs, architecture, detection, testing and communication.
Up-to-date, reliable and resilient ICT systems, protocols and tools
Use proportionate, reliable systems with sufficient capacity and resilience for stressed conditions.
Identify and classify business functions, assets and dependencies
Identify, classify and document ICT-supported functions, roles, assets and dependencies; review yearly.
Identify ICT risk sources, threats and vulnerabilities
Continuously identify risk sources and assess threats and vulnerabilities; review risk scenarios yearly.
Non-microenterprises assess risk on each major change to infrastructure, processes or procedures.
Identify and map all information and ICT assets
Identify all assets incl. remote sites and map critical asset configurations and interdependencies.
Identify processes dependent on ICT third-party providers
Document processes relying on providers and interconnections supporting critical functions.
Maintain and update asset and dependency inventories
Keep inventories updated periodically and after every major change.
Annual risk assessment of legacy ICT systems
Non-microenterprises assess legacy systems yearly and before and after connecting new technology.
Continuously monitor and control ICT security and functioning
Monitor and control ICT systems and reduce ICT risk impact with security tools and policies.
Design ICT security for resilience and data CIA
Implement measures ensuring resilience and data CIA at rest, in use and in transit.
ICT solutions secure transfers and prevent data loss and unauthorised access
Secure data transfer, minimise corruption, loss and unauthorised access, and protect against data management risks.
Develop and document an information security policy protecting data and assets, incl. customers'.
Network and infrastructure management with isolation capability
Manage networks risk-based and be able to sever or segment connections to stop contagion.
Limit physical and logical access to what is required
Restrict access to legitimate, approved functions with sound access rights administration.
Strong authentication and cryptographic key protection
Implement strong authentication and key protection with encryption based on classification and risk.
Record, test, assess, approve, implement and verify changes in a controlled way.
Maintain documented policies for patches and updates.
Prompt detection of anomalous activities and single points of failure
Detect anomalies, network performance issues and incidents, identify single points of failure and test detection.
Layered detection, alert thresholds and response triggers
Use multiple control layers with alert thresholds that trigger response and automatic alerts.
Resources to monitor user activity, anomalies and incidents
Dedicate sufficient resources to monitor user activity and ICT incidents, especially cyber-attacks.
Data reporting service providers check trade reports
Check trade reports for completeness and errors and request retransmission.
Put in place an ICT BC policy, standalone or within the overall BC policy.
BC arrangements, containment, impact estimation and crisis communication
Ensure continuity of critical functions, swift response, containment, early impact estimates and crisis communication.
ICT response and recovery plans with independent audit review
Implement response and recovery plans, independently reviewed by internal audit (non-microenterprises).
Maintain and test plans for outsourced critical functions
Maintain and periodically test BC plans, notably for functions outsourced to providers.
Conduct a BIA of severe disruptions and design assets with redundancy for critical components.
Annual testing of BC and recovery plans and crisis communication
Test at least yearly and after major changes, incl. cyber-attack and switchover scenarios; review plans.
Non-microenterprises have a crisis management function with internal and external communication procedures.
Keep accessible records of activities before and during disruption events.
CSDs provide BC test results to authorities
Give competent authorities copies of BC test results.
Report annual costs and losses of major incidents on request
Non-microenterprises report estimated aggregated annual costs and losses of major incidents on request.
Backup policies and restoration and recovery procedures
Document backup scope and frequency by criticality and restoration methods.
Backup systems activated without compromising security; periodic testing
Set up backup systems that preserve data security and test procedures periodically.
Restore from systems separated from the source and protected against unauthorised access.
Non-microenterprises keep redundant ICT capacity sufficient for business needs.
CSDs keep a secondary site with a distinct risk profile, equivalent capability and immediate staff access.
RTO and RPO for each function
Set recovery time and point objectives by function criticality and market impact.
Perform checks and reconciliations to ensure data integrity after recovery.
Capability to gather threat and vulnerability information
Have capabilities and staff to collect threat and vulnerability information and analyse impact.
Review causes and needed improvements after major incidents; report changes to authorities on request.
Feed lessons learned into risk assessment
Use testing, incident and supervisory lessons to update risk assessments and the framework.
Monitor effectiveness of the resilience strategy
Track strategy effectiveness, risk trends and cyber maturity.
Senior ICT staff report to management body yearly
Report findings and recommendations to the management body at least yearly.
ICT security awareness and resilience training for all staff
Run mandatory security awareness and resilience training for staff and senior management.
Non-microenterprises monitor technology developments to keep risk practices current.
Crisis communication plans for major incidents
Have plans to disclose major incidents or vulnerabilities to clients, counterparts and the public.
Communication policies for staff and external stakeholders
Adopt internal and external communication policies distinguishing staff roles.
Designated spokesperson for ICT incident communication
Assign at least one person to implement the communication strategy and act as spokesperson.
Exempted smaller entities maintain a simplified framework covering monitoring, detection, dependencies, continuity, testing and training.
